c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: The line sensors point down at the table. What do they actually notice at the edge?

B.text: That nothing is reflecting light back

C.text: The color of the floor below

c1.why: The sensor sends light down and listens for it coming back. Over the edge nothing comes back — that is all it knows.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: Why does the car have two of these sensors instead of one?

A.text: Two tell it which side the trouble is on

B.text: One is for black, one is for white

D.text: Two make it read twice as fast

c2.why: One sensor says "trouble". Two say "trouble on the left" or "trouble on the right" — and that is what lets the car pick an escape.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: At the edge of a table, what must the car do first?
c3.why: Turning at the edge swings a wheel out over the drop. Backing up first puts the whole car back on solid table.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: Both sensors are over the table top. What does the car do?
r1.why: That is the "all is well" branch, and 20 to both wheels is a slow, straight crawl.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: The front of the car reaches the edge. What happens?

D.text: It backs up for a third of a second, then checks again

r2.why: The escape branch reverses, holds that for 300ms, and then the loop comes round and reads the sensors again.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: Why is the turn amount random?

A.text: To use up the random block from Level 1

B.text: So the car looks more alive

C.text: So it does not head straight back to the same edge every time

D.text: Because the sensor gives a random number

r3.why: A fixed turn retraces the same path and finds the same edge. Varying it is what gets the car out into open table.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: What does this car do at the edge of the table?
r4.why: There is no branch for "no table". The car crawls forward whatever the sensors say.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: This car turns at the edge before it reverses, and sometimes a wheel goes over. Which change fixes it?

A.text: Use a longer pause on the turn

C.text: Put the reverse blocks before the turn

d1.why: The order is the bug. Reverse gets the car back onto the table; only then is it safe to turn.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: The car checks the edge once at start-up and then drives off it anyway. What is missing?
d2.why: The edge arrives later, not at start-up. A sensor has to be asked over and over for the answer to stay true.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Put the escape in the right order: 1 turn by a random amount · 2 reverse · 3 stop · 4 pause after each move
b1.why: Reverse, hold it, turn, hold it, then stop. Each move needs time or the next block wipes it out — and the next trip round the loop starts the creep again.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: You want the car to creep — slowly enough to stop in time. Which speed pair fits?
b2.why: Slow and equal. A fast crawl reaches the edge before the loop has had a chance to read it.
